query: Consider the following context: During the hot dip aluminum plating process, components such as sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates will come into long-term contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum and be corroded by the aluminum liquid, greatly reducing their service life. In that context, which material can be used for prepare parts for the dipping and plating equipment and protect the equipment from erosion, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Applying a tungsten-carbide-based cermet coating on steel roller surfaces used in hot dip aluminum plating equipment will significantly reduce molten aluminum corrosion and extend the service life of those components compared to uncoated steel rollers.
generation.material_initial_state: Steel substrates in standard roller geometry for hot dip aluminum plating lines, without protective coatings.
generation.intervention: Application of a tungsten-carbide-based cermet coating onto the steel substrates, for example using High-Velocity Oxy-Fuel (HVOF) thermal spraying.
generation.conditions: Extended immersion in molten aluminum at typical hot dip plating temperatures (approximately 680–750°C).
generation.structural_mediator: A dense, adherent cermet layer on the steel surface limiting chemical interaction and mechanical wear from molten aluminum.
generation.mechanism: The tungsten-carbide-based cermet forms a chemically stable, hard barrier that resists molten aluminum corrosion and wear, reducing surface degradation and preventing aluminum infiltration into the steel substrate.
generation.predicted_outcome: The tungsten-carbide-coated rollers will exhibit significantly lower mass loss due to reduced corrosion and wear, resulting in at least a moderate (e.g., two- to threefold) increase in their service life compared to uncoated steel rollers under identical conditions.
generation.baseline: Uncoated steel rollers in contact with molten aluminum, which typically suffer rapid mass loss and premature failure due to corrosion and erosion.
generation.boundary: Performance gains may diminish if coating application quality is suboptimal or if thermal/shock cycling exceeds recommended process limits for cermet coatings.
generation.uncertainty: The actual degree of lifespan extension may vary widely based on specific process details, such as coating thickness, substrate preparation, and operational parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare steel rollers with and without tungsten-carbide-based cermet coatings. Submerge both sets in molten aluminum at standard process temperatures for a set period (e.g., 72 hours) and measure their surface degradation, mass loss, and mechanical integrity over time.
measurements: Mass loss of coated versus uncoated rollers after immersion
Qualitative and quantitative analysis of corrosion or pitting on the roller surfaces
Hardness measurements before and after immersion
Microscopic examination of coating integrity and coating-substrate interface
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated rollers do not show a significant reduction in mass loss and improved integrity compared to the uncoated counterparts, the hypothesis is refuted.
